title: 3. Death of Partners and Sale of Partnership Firm
subtitle: Mode of Payment, Deceased Partner's Share of Profit, Joint Life Policy, Sale of Firm to a Company

questions.q: Death of a partner, like retirement, results in:
options: Automatic winding up of the business
Permanent suspension of all firm operations

questions.q: The main accounting difference between retirement and death of a partner is that, in case of death:
options: Accounts are generally prepared up to the date of death, which may fall in the middle of an accounting year
The firm must be compulsorily dissolved
No revaluation of assets and liabilities is required

questions.q: The amount due to a deceased partner is payable to their:
The mode of payment of the amount due to a deceased partner's executor may be:
options: Only in a single lump sum, by law
A lump sum or instalments, as agreed or provided in the partnership deed
Only after one full year from the date of death
Only through transfer of fixed assets

questions.q: The deceased partner's share of profit up to the date of death is generally ascertained on the basis of:
options: The firm's total capital on that date
Time basis or turnover/sales basis, as agreed
The average capital of all partners

questions.q: Under the time basis of ascertaining the deceased partner's share of profit, the previous year's profit is:
options: Apportioned in proportion to the period from the last Balance Sheet date to the date of death
Distributed equally among all partners, regardless of time

questions.q: Under the turnover/sales basis of ascertaining a deceased partner's share of profit, the estimate is based on:
options: The proportion of sales achieved up to the date of death, compared to total sales of the previous year
The number of days the partner worked, regardless of sales

questions.q: A Joint Life Policy (JLP) is taken out by a partnership firm primarily to:
options: Provide funds to pay the deceased partner's dues without straining the firm's working capital
Reduce the firm's income tax liability permanently
Increase the market value of the firm's goodwill
Avoid the need to calculate a new profit-sharing ratio

questions.q: The premium paid on a Joint Life Policy may be treated in the firm's books either as:
options: An expense (charged to Profit and Loss Account) or as an asset (shown in the Balance Sheet)
Always as a loan to partners

questions.q: When the JLP premium is treated as an expense (revenue method), the policy amount received on a partner's death is credited to:
options: All partners' Capital Accounts, in their profit-sharing ratio
Only the deceased partner's Capital Account

questions.q: When a Joint Life Policy Account is maintained (premium treated as an asset), the surrender value is normally shown in the firm's:
options: Profit and Loss Account every year
Balance Sheet, as an asset, until maturity or claim

questions.q: On the death of a partner, if the Joint Life Policy matures, the excess of the amount received over its book/surrender value is treated as:
options: A liability to the deceased partner's executor only
Profit, distributed among all partners in their profit-sharing ratio
A loss to be borne by continuing partners alone

questions.q: The sale of a partnership firm to a company typically involves:
options: Compulsory insolvency proceedings against all partners
Permanent closure of the business with no consideration received
Liquidation of all assets for cash only, with no transfer to any entity
Transfer of the firm's assets and liabilities to the company in exchange for purchase consideration

questions.q: Purchase consideration, when a partnership firm is sold to a company, generally refers to:
options: The price agreed to be paid by the company for taking over the business of the firm
The firm's total profit for the current year
The capital originally contributed by the partners

questions.q: One common method of computing purchase consideration is the:
options: Net Payment Method or Net Asset Method

questions.q: Under the Net Asset Method of computing purchase consideration, it is calculated as:
options: The firm's average profit multiplied by years of purchase
Total of all assets, regardless of whether taken over
Agreed value of assets taken over, minus liabilities taken over

questions.q: On sale of the firm to a company, a Realisation Account is prepared to record:
options: Only the purchase consideration received in cash
The transfer and disposal of the firm's assets and liabilities, and to ascertain profit or loss on sale
Only the goodwill of the firm

questions.q: When a partnership firm is sold to a company, purchase consideration may be received by the partners in the form of:
options: Only as a loan from the company
Cash, shares, debentures, or a combination of these, as agreed

questions.q: Profit or loss on realisation, when a firm is sold to a company, is distributed among partners in their:
options: Capital ratio, irrespective of profit-sharing ratio

questions.q: The main purpose of a Joint Life Policy, from the firm's perspective, is risk management against:
options: Fluctuations in the market price of goods
The financial strain of paying a deceased partner's dues suddenly

questions.q: If a Joint Life Policy is taken on the joint lives of all partners, the claim normally becomes receivable:
options: On the death of any one partner (first death)
Only after 20 years, regardless of any death
Only when all partners have died

questions.q: The amount due to a deceased partner, to the extent unpaid, is generally transferred to a:
On death of a partner, the gaining ratio of the continuing partners is used, similar to retirement, to:
options: Determine how much each continuing partner compensates for the deceased partner's share of goodwill
Determine the deceased partner's final drawings

questions.q: In the absence of any agreement, interest payable to a deceased partner's executor on an unpaid balance (Section 37, Partnership Act) follows the same provision applicable to:
A life policy taken out jointly on the lives of all partners, rather than separate policies for each, is known as a:
On the death of a partner, profit or loss on revaluation of assets and liabilities is shared by:
options: All partners, including the deceased partner up to the date of death, in the old profit-sharing ratio
Equally among continuing partners, regardless of ratio

questions.q: When a firm sells its business to a limited company, the firm itself is referred to as the:
The company that takes over the business of the firm is referred to as the:
If the purchase consideration exceeds the net assets taken over by the company, the excess is treated, in the firm's books, as:
If the purchase consideration is less than the net assets taken over, the shortfall represents, in the firm's books:
The deceased partner's Capital Account balance, after all adjustments, represents the amount payable to:
options: The executor or legal heirs of the deceased partner

questions.q: On the death of a partner during the accounting year, reserves and accumulated profits in the Balance Sheet are distributed among:
options: Equally, regardless of the old ratio
All partners, including the deceased partner, in the old profit-sharing ratio

questions.q: A Joint Life Policy Reserve Account, where maintained, is used to:
options: Accumulate funds against fluctuations in the surrender value of the policy
Replace the Capital Accounts of partners

questions.q: Where no Joint Life Policy exists, the cash required to pay a deceased partner's executor is usually arranged by:
options: The continuing partners, from the firm's funds or by introducing additional capital/loans
Compulsory dissolution and sale of all assets
Writing off the amount as a bad debt

questions.q: Regarding the deceased partner's executor becoming a partner in the firm:
options: The executor inherits full managerial control of the firm
The executor does not become a partner merely by receiving the deceased partner's dues
The executor must be a chartered accountant
The executor automatically becomes a full partner

questions.q: The legal basis for interest payable to a deceased partner's representative on an unsettled balance, similar to a retiring partner, is found in:
Under the Net Payment Method of computing purchase consideration, it is the sum of:
options: The firm's total liabilities taken over
All forms of payment (cash, shares, debentures, etc.) actually paid or payable by the purchasing company
Only the value of shares issued

questions.q: In the Realisation Account prepared on sale of the firm, assets transferred to the account are recorded at their:
options: Book values, before any revaluation for the sale
Nil, since they are being disposed of

questions.q: The balance of the Realisation Account (profit or loss), on sale of the firm to a company, is ultimately transferred to the:
options: Partners' Capital Accounts, in their profit-sharing ratio

questions.q: Death of a partner is similar to retirement in that both situations require:
options: Settlement of the outgoing partner's share of profits, goodwill and revaluation gains/losses
Conversion of the firm into a company
Admission of a replacement partner within 30 days
